Subject: Increased 5xx/429 + timeouts — we need an ETA

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing elevated 5xx and 429 rates against our inference calls to the 'redwood-generation-us' endpoint around 08:50 PDT this morning. Current numbers from our telemetry: ~18-22% 5xx (mostly 500/504), ~12-16% 429s, and a steady increase in client-side timeouts. This is affecting multiple customer flows (batch scoring and live chat).

Quick details:
- Region: us-west (us)
- Model: redwood-compact-13b (pinned)
- First spike observed: 08:50 PDT
- Rolling error sample attached (snippet)

Our mobile clients are aggressively retrying and we suspect a retry amplification. Can you confirm you’re seeing the same on your side, and share a mitigation ETA? This is impacting revenue-facing paths — we need a firm timeline.

Thanks,
Tim

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased 5xx/429 + timeouts — preliminary root cause & mitigations

Tim / Marissa — quick technical update from infra: we are observing a retry-amplification loop combined with a transient GPU memory pressure event on a subset of nodes servicing redwood-compact-13b. Short summary:

- Symptom: surge of small, rapid retries from clients creating queue buildup at the gateway. When backend latency spikes (500s/504s), clients retry which increases queue length and pushes more requests into slow paths — classic feedback loop.
- Probable triggers: a routine model checkpoint job coincided with a higher-than-usual request burst; a handful of nodes hit GPU OOM and fell back to slower CPU inference, increasing latency.

Immediate mitigations we’re executing now (timeline in parentheses):
1) Edge reject-policy: install a short-lived filter to reject immediate retries (return 429 with Retry-After) for aggressive client patterns. This prevents the amplification (ETA: 20 minutes).
2) Temporarily scale up the dedicated pool for the pin (add 4 nodes) and drain slower nodes (ETA: 35 minutes for scale-up, draining concurrent).
3) Enable conservative prefix/KV cache for Hippo traffic to reduce per-request compute (ETA: 15–25 minutes).
4) Apply a hotfix to the scheduler to avoid co-scheduling heavy checkpoint jobs during peak traffic windows (deploy in next 4 hours, post-incident rollout).

Attachments: diagnostic-logs-20260421.txt (contains request ids and sample traces). I’ve included two example traces showing the retry loop and where latency jumped.

Metrics checkpoint: we see error rate trend starting to stabilize in regions not impacted by the OOM nodes; global aggregation still showing the spike until scaling completes.

I’ll post another update once the edge policy is live.

—Rishi
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

Tim — below is a proposed customer-facing note you can send to your internal stakeholders; Marissa / Rishi / Sean please edit for technical accuracy before we send.

Hi Tim / Hippo Health team,

We’re investigating elevated error rates and timeouts affecting inference requests to the us region that began at ~08:50 PDT today. Impact: intermittent 500/504 and 429 responses causing some failed requests and client timeouts.

What we’re doing right now:
- Deploying an edge-level reject policy to prevent retry amplification (reduces load on backends).
- Provisioning additional compute capacity to replace nodes affected by transient memory pressure.
- Enabling conservative prefix/KV caching for your traffic to lower per-request compute.

What you can expect:
- Short-term ETA: we expect measurable improvement within 30–45 minutes; full normalization in the next 2–3 hours as nodes drain and the pool warms.
- We will follow up with a post-incident report including root cause and long-term fixes.

If you need a phone bridge or direct Slack channel, we can open one. Apologies for the disruption — we’re prioritizing Hippo Health traffic until resolved.

Thanks,
Marissa on behalf of Redwood Inference Ops

To: Tim Wilson <tim.wilson@hippohealth.com>, Hippo Health Support <support@hippohealth.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: mitigation completed — metrics improving (follow-up report forthcoming)

Tim — final update before we prepare the post-incident report.

Summary: we implemented the edge reject-policy and scaled the dedicated pool; we also enabled prefix caching for Hippo traffic and drained the nodes that experienced GPU memory pressure. As of 12:50 PDT the error rates have fallen significantly. Latest aggregated metrics: 5xx ~0.8%, 429 ~1.1%, latency median back to baseline for most request sizes.

What happened (short): a confluence of a transient GPU memory pressure event on several nodes and client retry amplification led to the spike.

What we did: edge reject-policy, short-term capacity increase, prefix caching, and scheduler hotfix planned to prevent checkpoint jobs from running during peak traffic windows.

Next steps:
- We’ll send a detailed post-incident report (timeline, RCA, and long-term remediations) by EOD tomorrow.
- I’ll loop in our solutions engineering team to review retry/backoff guidance with Hippo engineers to avoid aggressive client retries.

If you’d like an executive call or Slack bridge, I can set it up. Thank you for your patience; sorry again for the disruption.

—Marissa Cole
